title: Dictionaries
summary: Tables keyed by names (strings) instead of numbers: instant lookup by key. Settings, inventories, caches, and 'sets' are all dictionaries.

details.heading: Dot vs bracket
details.body: `t.key` works only for keys that are valid identifiers (letters/digits/underscore, not starting with a digit, not a reserved word). Keys with spaces or special characters need brackets: `t["max health"]`.

details.heading: No order, no length
details.body: `pairs` order is unspecified, and `#t` does not count dictionary entries. Keep a separate counter or an array if you need order/count.

explanation.whatItIs: A dictionary maps names to values: 'health' → 100, 'sword' → true. You ask for a key and get the value instantly, without searching through a list.
explanation.whyItExists: Named lookup is everywhere: configuration, player stats, caches, permission flags. Dictionaries make those O(1).
whenToUse: Named data bundles: `local playerData = { coins = 0, level = 1 }`
Sets: `local banned = { [userId] = true }` then `if banned[id] then`
Caches: remember expensive computations by key
Dispatch tables: `handlers[commandName](player, args)` instead of if/elseif chains
whenNotToUse: When you need order (leaderboard positions, turn order) — use an array, or array + dictionary combo
When keys are sequential integers anyway — that's just an array
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
stats = {
    health = 100,
    mana   = 40,
    armor  = 25,
}

"What's health?" --> stats.health --> 100
```
A dictionary is a row of labeled drawers. You don't open them one by one — you go straight to the label.
tips: The set pattern `t[value] = true` gives near-instant membership tests — much faster than scanning an array with `table.find`
Use `pairs` (or plain `for k, v in t` in Luau) to walk all entries
`next(t) == nil` tests whether a dictionary is empty
commonMistakes: Expecting `pairs` to return entries in the order they were added
Key typos creating a second key: `statis.health` vs `stats.health`

examples.title: The set pattern: instant membership checks
examples.code:
local vip = {
    [1234] = true,
    [9876] = true,
}

local function isVip(userId)
    return vip[userId] == true
end

print(isVip(1236))   --> false
print(isVip(9876))   --> true
examples.whyItWorks: Keys are looked up directly — no loop needed. This scales to millions of entries just as fast.

examples.title: Command dispatch table
examples.code:
local handlers = {
    heal = function(player) print("Healing " .. player.Name) end,
    kick = function(player) print("Kicking " .. player.Name) end,
}

local function runCommand(player, command)
    local fn = handlers[command]
    if fn then
        fn(player)
    else
        warn("Unknown command:", command)
    end
end
examples.whyItWorks: The dictionary replaces a growing if/elseif chain. Adding a command = adding one line.
